summary: Agvan Dorzhiev was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a Geshey Lharampa degree at Drepung Gomang Dratsang, where he studied in 1873 and 1880–1888. He taught the 13th Dalai Lama and founded Atsagat Datsan in 1913.

Ahmad Hasan Dani specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University under A. S. Altekar, trained under Mortimer Wheeler, and attended the University of London under K. de B. Codrington. He held major posts at Dhaka, Peshawar, and Quaid-i-Azam universities.

Aiko Okoshi worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University until 1975 and was appointed a full-time lecturer at Kindai University in 1990.

Aileen Dansken Ross was an Indology scholar who studied at the London School of Economics and the University of Chicago (MA, PhD). She taught sociology at the University of Toronto (1942–1945) and served at McGill University as lecturer, assistant professor, and professor (1964–1970).

Ajahn Amaro is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied psychology and physiology at Bedford College before training under Ajahn Chah and Ajahn Sumedho. He served as co-abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery (~1996–2010) and became abbot of Amaravati Buddhist Monastery around 2010.

Ajahn Brahm specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Emmanuel College, Cambridge, and trained under Boonman Poonyathiro and Ajahn Chah. He became the abbot of Bodhinyana Monastery around 1996.

Ajahn Khemadhammo is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the Drama Centre London from around 1963 to 1966 and pursued traditional training under Ajahn Chah from around 1972 to 1977.

Ajahn Pasanno is a Buddhist studies scholar who received traditional training under Ajahn Chah from around 1974 to 1982. He served as the founding co-abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery from around 1996 to 2018.

Ajahn Sucitto specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied English and American literature at the University of Warwick (~1968–1971) and became a disciple of Ajahn Sumedho in 1977. He served as abbot of Chithurst Buddhist Monastery from 1992 to 2014.

Ajahn Sumedho is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at the University of California, Berkeley, and studied under Ajahn Chah. He served as the abbot of Wat Pa Nanachat in 1975 and as abbot of Amaravati Buddhist Monastery from 1984 to 2010.

Ajay Verma specializes in philosophy and Indology. He completed an M.Phil and PhD at the University of Delhi between 1997 and 2004, and was appointed Associate Professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2005.

Ajit Ranjan Bhattacharyya was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a pupil under Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya. He held a post at the University of Calcutta as an Ex-Puranchand Nahar Fellow.
Akhil Rajeev P works in the fields of computational studies and Indology. He has held positions at the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing and the Indian Heritage Language Computing Group.

Akifumi Naito specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University and Honganji Sōgakuin, and with Gadjin Nagao. His posts include assistant professor at Shinshu Institute of Doctrinal Studies, former associate professor at Ryukoku University, and lecturer at Kyoto Women's University.

Akihiko Akamatsu is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Yuichi Kajiyama at Kyoto University and completed a PhD at the University of Paris/Sorbonne Nouvelle. He held posts as associate professor at Kyushu University (1987) and professor and vice-president at Kyoto University.

Akihiro Oda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University. He also served on the faculty at Otani University, attested as a full-time lecturer in 1992 and as Professor of Buddhist Studies in 2013.
Akiko Kikuchi works in Buddhist studies and other fields. She studied as a research student at Minobusan University (attested 2026) and was appointed Professor at Musashino University in 2022.
Akiko Murakawa is an Indologist who studied under supervisors Harry Falk, Gerhard Ehlers, Masato Fujii, and Muneo Tokunaga, and teachers Werner Knobl, Yasuke Ikari, and Kazuhiko Yoshida.

Akiko Walley is a scholar of Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Aoyama Gakuin University and Harvard University, and held a post at the University of Oregon from 2009 to 2016.

Akimichi Eda works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Dr. phil. at the University of Marburg under doctoral supervisor Michael Hahn, and also studied under Katsumi Mimaki and Tsultrim Kelsang Khangkar.
